citation: Toyohara J., Zhou W. (2026) Cost-Optimal Decarbonization Pathways for Data Centers in Japan: A Bottom-Up Model Integrating Location, Energy Systems, and Carbon Pricing. Energies 19(10), 2485. https://doi.org/10.3390/en19102485

dedupe_keys.name: dc decom cost optimal decarbonisation pathways for data centres in japan

description: DC-DECOM is a multi-regional bottom-up linear programming model of Japan's data centre industry for 2024 to 2040, written by Jin Toyohara and Weisheng Zhou as companion code to their article in Energies (2026, volume 19, article 2485). It chooses where to site data centre load across five regions over 17 years and how to supply it with a mix of technologies, with a dynamic power usage effectiveness module calibrated to regional temperature, a carbon accounting module and three scenarios: reference, centralised carbon-neutral and regionally distributed carbon-neutral. Input parameters (global values, regional data and 96-hour temperature profiles) are included as CSV, and post-processing decomposes cost into cooling, renewable energy, carbon and siting channels. Coverage: Japan, five regions, 2024 to 2040. Format and access: Python code using PuLP on GitHub under the MIT licence, with data under CC BY 4.0, archived on Zenodo (v1.0.1, May 2026) with 14 reproducibility tests. Caveats: an individual research artefact; the authors note it is a reference implementation whose default parameters reproduce the paper's results only qualitatively; no grid network constraints. Simulation uses: capacity planning and optimisation of data centre siting and energy supply under carbon prices and warming, and climate adaptation of cooling demand. Related records: OpenDC and CloudSim Plus simulate operations inside a data centre, not the national system.
